approval_note: The committee cannot approve. PASS means no auditor found anything to veto on its own axis with the evidence it was given. Reading that as approval is a caller's policy -- pre-registration.md 6a -- and its error rate is unmeasured.

auditors.confidence_note: Everything the strategy reads (quotes, sizes, strikes, expiry_session, ctx.session, held assets, working orders) is current-state data available at the decision bar; there is no self-carried state derived from later data, no reference to scoring/split/seed/calendar, and no use of session range or session close mid-session.

The gate is the authoritative corrected test and it REJECTED (p=0.099 > q=0.05, well above the 1e-4 floor); the metric is not degenerate (sortino over 105 sessions with 39 downside sessions and 151 trades), and the sharp divergence of the uncorrected/BH/Holm (49 discoveries) and deflation (clears_selection_bar) views is explicitly explained as a miscalibrated per-trial FAR column and a moments-only margin rather than a rate — but I could not see per-session returns to rule out that the high skew (2.96) and kurtosis (7.95) hide concentration in a few sessions, could not interpret the unlabeled 'significance: 58.86' field that sits oddly beside the gate's p=0.099, and cannot see how many prior campaigns preceded this one.

The evidence does not include a clean-surface baseline comparison for this strategy, so I could not independently confirm that the 151 trades reflect planted violations rather than a self-inflicted spread artifact (the strategy's commission-adjusted touched-size accounting looks correct, which is the main protection against that failure mode); the validation split was also not run, which is off my axis but is visible in the record.

reasons: breadth_by_hour_utc is narrow: only 6 of 21 hours are positive (28.6%) while 15 hours are negative, and the minority of positive hours carries the entire result — the four dominant hours (01, 07, 13, 19) contribute ~4429 gross versus a net total of ~4414, meaning the majority of trading hours collectively subtract profit.

The four dominant profitable hours (01, 07, 13, 19) are spaced exactly 6 hours apart, with secondary earners at 10 and 16 (also 6 hours apart), a suspiciously regular pattern with no stated rationale given for why these specific hours would persist — this matches the 'fitted to sample' veto criterion alongside the narrow hourly breadth.
auditors.confidence_note: Cannot see the strategy's rules or any rationale linking the 4 dominant hours to persistent market regimes; the seasonality_caveat notes per-cell counts are tiny (151 trades over 21 hours ≈ 7 avg), so I cannot distinguish genuine narrowing from noise, but by the letter of the 'few periods carry the result' criterion the hourly distribution is a veto.
